tweet.text:
❗️ #THORChain has never been strictly decentralized

@THORChain comparing itself to decentralized L1s like BTC and ETH does not hold. Do not enable criminals — or put the industry at risk — just to take swap fees on stolen funds.

1️⃣ Custody: TSS vaults ≠ base-layer consensus

On BTC/ETH, users control assets with their own keys. Miners/validators order and include txs. They never hold user funds. The worst a single miner can do is refuse to include your tx. They cannot send your coins.

Every THORChain outbound (vault → user/attacker) has to be actively produced by the current active set via a GG20 TSS threshold signature. During a swap, funds sit in a TSS vault jointly controlled by those nodes.

Releasing stolen funds is an active signing event, not “neutral ordering we cannot stop.” As @star_okx put it: from a custody view it is an intermediary between users and native chains. Distributed centralized custody is not decentralization.
